name: Christ Church Cathedral (Fredericton)
scope: The extant sandstone Christ Church Cathedral in Fredericton, with the cruciform nave, low aisles, east sanctuary tracing, side porch, crossing belfry and tall post-fire spire.
era: Extant Gothic Revival cathedral with the rebuilt spire after the 1911 fire

originalReview.notes: The winter view shows the brown-grey ashlar of the east sanctuary and adjacent wing, the steep teal roofs, pale Caen stone window tracery, angled buttresses, tower corner pinnacles and the long dark ribbed spire and cross.

review.method: Exact published Qualla original with creator release and preserved original native upload log
review.notes: The exact 2005 Qualla original matches the native Commons file and the transfer retains the initial photographer declaration and public-domain release. The Qualla 1909 image predates the 1911 fire and its native location metadata is inconsistent. Only the post-restoration 2005 photo supplies visual reference.
